inert: plan only: no call was executed, nothing was published, no network or clock was used
notClaimed: no execution, publication, network, T7 or clock; no canonicality, completeness, delivery, latency or admission evidence; Q1/Q2 unresolved, no dedup/identity policy chosen

resumeLive.condition: live may resume at H+1 only after every planned call completed within maxBytes and canonicality was re-verified by the executor; this plan proves neither

rules.budget: if calls > maxCalls emit only the first maxCalls calls (TRUNCATED_CALL_BUDGET) and state the first uncovered (range, filterset) and the uncovered block range; maxBytes is an executor stop limit (no volume estimate)
rules.chunking: each segment split ascending into ranges of <= maxChunkBlocks blocks; overlap before gap; every filterset per range in manifest order; one call per (range, filterset); range and call counts are computed arithmetically and only emitted calls are generated
rules.gap: read [C+1, H] only when 1 <= H-C <= maxGapBlocks; H-C = 0 plans the overlap only; H-C > maxGapBlocks plans nothing (GAP_EXCEEDS_CAP)
rules.historyLimit: nothing below max(0, C-L+1) is ever requested; reorgs deeper than L, provider log-history retention and pruning are not detectable here; an executor that cannot serve a range must report UNKNOWN, never empty
rules.integers: block numbers <= 2^53-2 so C+1 and H+1 are exact; caps are safe integers >= 1; maxCalls <= 10000 bounds the output; counts are exact decimal strings (BigInt)
rules.overlap: re-read [max(0, C-L+1), C]: L = operator-declared lookbackBlocks (>=1, <= maxGapBlocks); the checkpoint block itself is always re-read
rules.reconciliation: UNKNOWN_NEEDS_RECONCILIATION (no ranges) when: checkpointBlockHashAtHead null or != checkpoint.blockHash; removedLogsSeen true or null; H < C; H == C with a different hash; head observed before the checkpoint was recorded
rules.resumeLive: live may resume at H+1 only after every planned call completed within maxBytes and canonicality was re-verified by the executor; this plan proves neither
